resources.string: The app now runs on Android 8 and 9 too.\nUnder-the-hood updates for newer Android versions.
Dates can now be typed. Open Date range in step 2 and tap the pencil to enter them with the keyboard; the calendar icon takes you back to the calendar.

New: Trips. Step 3 now has a Trips tab listing every trip more than 50 km from home, door to door, with dates, distance and how you travelled. Tap a trip to see it on the map; tick trips to export just those.
Filters and export choices are now remembered for the next file.
Distance totals no longer count activities twice in merged files.
Fixed a crash when opening a second file on some phones.
With “Color by day” on, KML and GeoJSON exports now keep each day\'s color, one line per day, just like the map.

See the total distance for the dates you picked right in the Movement row, and a Total line when several movement types are selected.\nWhen only a few movement types are unticked, the Movement row now reads \"All except …\", so the distance and places count stay in view.

Redesigned: see which file is open, simpler date filters, a new calendar, and a dark theme that matches the map.
Color your track by day and browse days by month; tap a day to see where you were.
Big location histories now export much faster without running out of memory, and the map draws them smoothly, in full detail when you zoom in.
Loading progress now fills evenly instead of crawling, then jumping.

Redesigned: see which file is open, simpler date filters, a new calendar, and a dark theme that matches the map.\nColor your track by day and browse days by month; tap a day to see where you were.\nLoading progress now fills evenly instead of crawling, then jumping.

Export your places, not just your track: where you were, how often and for how long — in all four formats.
Filter by time of day: only your mornings, or only your nights, on the local clock.
A quieter map, where the track builds up along the streets you walk most.
CSV local times are now correct abroad, and exports can go straight to another app. Still no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

Fixed local times in CSV exports. Points recorded abroad were stamped with your home time zone, so a trip could be off by hours. They now carry the time zone that was actually in effect where you were.
Exports can go straight to another app — mail, chat, a map — instead of being saved as a file first.
Older Takeout exports now keep the real place names and addresses they contain.
Everything still runs entirely on your device: no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

Fixed a crash on Android 10–13: picking a quick day range, opening the date picker or saving an export could close the app instead of doing the job.\nThe map is now shut down cleanly when you leave the screen, which fixes a rarer crash on the way out.\nEverything still runs entirely on your device: no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

New: choose what to export, not just when. Step 2 breaks your date range down by movement — walking, cycling, driving, transport, flights — with trips and distance for each.
Tick the kinds you want and only those go into the file.
"Only while moving" drops points recorded while you were stopped; "Skip repeated points" collapses identical coordinates.
Everything still runs entirely on your device: no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

New: tell me what to add. After an export — and at the bottom of Help — you can open a short request form, tick the features you want and send them via GitHub or email.
The app sends nothing by itself: the draft opens in your browser or mail app, and you decide what goes in it.
CSV exports now carry local time and the UTC offset next to UTC time.
Everything still runs entirely on your device: no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

Maintenance update: the app now uses the latest Google Play billing components, as required by Google.\nThe tip jar is more reliable — it reconnects to Google Play on its own if the connection drops.\nNo changes to importing, filtering or exporting. Everything still runs entirely on your device: no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

Large Timeline files now import reliably. The app streams your data instead of loading the whole file into memory, so even very large exports (100 MB and up) no longer fail with an out-of-memory error.\nFaster imports that use far less memory.\nMore accurate progress bar, and the file size shown during import now matches what your file manager reports.
